Ransomware gang claims attack on hospital chain

The Akira ransomware group has claimed responsibility for a cyberattack on a regional hospital chain, listing the organisation on its data leak site on Tuesday and threatening to publish stolen patient records.

The hospital chain confirmed it detected unauthorised access to its network last week and has since taken several systems offline as a precaution. Emergency departments remain open, but some elective procedures were postponed while investigators work to restore services.

Security researchers said the group has increasingly targeted the healthcare sector over the past year, exploiting unpatched VPN appliances to gain initial access. Organisations are urged to apply vendor updates and enable multi-factor authentication on all remote access services.

The incident has been reported to the national cyber agency, which is assisting with the response.
